directions.name: Two halves of one name
directions.identity: The name says the shop is two things, a boulangerie and a pâtisserie, and the listed items are exactly one of each: a croissant and a tarte aux pommes. The design gives each half the same weight.

techniques.why: The shape comes from the name's two halves: two tall panels with fully rounded tops, one per half, repeated small for the ledger labels.
Hours and area are the only practical facts, so they must be complete and readable rather than decorative.

hero.choice: Two tall round-topped panels side by side under the full name: the left panel reads Boulangerie over クロワッサン, the right Pâtisserie over タルト・オ・ポム; no picture.
hero.why: The first screen states the shop's two sides and the one item listed for each, which is all the facts support.

product_visual.choice: Each item appears only as its name inside its panel, in Japanese, with no description, price or picture.
product_visual.why: The fixture gives item names and nothing else, so anything more would be invented.

typography.choice: A high-contrast Latin serif for Boulangerie and Pâtisserie at display size, Japanese Gothic for the two item names and the ledger.
typography.why: The French words are the shop's identity and carry the display face; the item names and facts must stay plain to read.

palette.choice: Pale sage-grey ground, near-black text, one warm panel and one cool panel, and a baked-crust brown accent for the two French words.
palette.why: Two panel tones mark the two halves of the name; the crust accent belongs to both bread and tart without using the usual cream and brown.

section_rhythm.choice: Name, then the two panels as the hero, then a short ledger and footer; the eye moves left panel, right panel, then down to hours.
section_rhythm.why: With four facts the honest page is short; the pairing is the one idea, so it gets the whole first screen.

sections.purpose: Full name and one anchor to the hours and area.
The two round-topped panels with one item name each.
Hours and address as label and value rows.

navigation.choice: One anchor from the header to the hours and area; nothing else, because nothing else exists to link to.
navigation.why: A menu or contact link would promise content the facts do not have.

mobile.choice: On a phone the two panels stack, Boulangerie first, each full width and shorter; the ledger follows as two rows.
mobile.why: Side-by-side panels would squeeze the French words; stacking keeps them at display size.
mobile.desktop: The two panels stand side by side at equal width under the name, filling the first screen.

implementation.choice: Grid for the two panels and ledger, large border-radius for the round tops, solid colour bands, horizontal text.
implementation.why: Round tops are border-radius, which the allowlist permits; no pseudo-element or clip-path is needed.

strengths: Buildable with the current CSS; the existing brief relies on pseudo-elements and a sticky-like label, both refused by the allowlist.
Its idea comes from the shop's own name and items instead of an abstract curve.
weaknesses: A very short page with no pictures; it can feel thin.
Two equal panels risk reading as a menu board rather than a shop identity.

directions.name: When and where, first
directions.identity: A shop known so far only by its name, two items, its hours and its area. This direction treats the hours as the strongest fact and builds a calm, dark page around when the shop is open.

techniques.why: The hours are the one fact every visitor needs; here the ledger is promoted into the first screen instead of closing the page.
A dark ground with one lighter band separates the opening facts from the items without any lines or shapes.

hero.choice: Information first: 10:00〜18:00 set as the largest element on a dark ground, the name above it in small Latin serif, and 名古屋市千種区 beneath it.
hero.why: For a shop with so few facts, being clear about when and where it is open is the most useful first impression.

product_visual.choice: The two items sit together on one line on the lighter band, クロワッサン and タルト・オ・ポム, separated by a thin rule.
product_visual.why: Neither item is described as the signature, so they are shown as equals in a single line.

typography.choice: Tabular Gothic numerals at display size for the hours, a small Latin serif for the name, Gothic for everything else.
typography.why: The hours are numbers, so the display type is a clear numeral; the French name stays small so it does not compete.

palette.choice: Deep ink-teal ground with warm off-white text, a lighter slate band for the items, and a muted gold accent only on the hours.
palette.why: A dark ground sets this direction apart from pastry clichés and from the existing lilac brief; gold marks only the hours, the page's one emphasis.

section_rhythm.choice: Hours and area in the first screen, then the items band, then the full address and footer; the eye drops straight down a single centred column.
section_rhythm.why: A single column with one emphasis fits a page this short and keeps the hours as the anchor.

sections.purpose: The hours at display size with the area beneath.
One line with the two item names on the lighter band.
The full address and hours as a short ledger.

navigation.choice: No navigation links at all: the page is one short column and every fact is visible within two screens.
navigation.why: Anchors would only point a few hundred pixels down; leaving them out keeps the header to the name.

mobile.choice: On a phone the hours stay at display size on one line, scaled to fit, with the area beneath; the items line wraps into two lines.
mobile.why: The hours must not break across lines, or the lead loses its point.
mobile.desktop: A centred column about 640 px wide on the dark ground, with generous space above and below the hours.

implementation.choice: One centred grid column, solid bands, horizontal text, a font size step for the hours at each breakpoint.
implementation.why: Nothing beyond the allowlist is used; fitting the hours on one phone line is done with breakpoints, not viewport units.

strengths: Puts the two facts a visitor needs in the first screen; the existing brief left them in a footer.
Buildable today, without pseudo-elements or sticky positioning.
weaknesses: Little brand character beyond the dark palette and the French name.
Leading with hours is unusual and may read as a notice rather than a shop.
